Lead source: self-serve signup (trial credits) -> reached out to AE after hitting errors.

Snapshot: SMB SaaS company building an in-app assistant + doc search for customers. Light steady traffic (10-20 qps) with periodic marketing and onboarding spikes (observed bursts up to ~70 concurrent requests over 5-10 minutes). Primary ask: hosted API that "plays nice" with spikes — minimize 429s, predictable quotas, clear retry guidance, and a straightforward path to short-term burst increases for promotions.

Key pain: first week after signup they triggered a product announcement email that drove a spike; their self-serve default quota returned many 429s. Devs implemented naive retry loop -> client-perceived latency and duplicate requests; worried about bad UX. Quote from CTO via call: "We can't have our onboarding convert flows fail when we run a promo — 429s kill conversion."

Technical requirements / targets (from discovery call):
- Typical baseline: 10-20 concurrent requests, 1-2k tokens/min average.
- Spikes: up to ~60-80 concurrent requests for 3-15 minutes during campaigns.
- Latency SLO: < 400ms p50 for short-turn prompts; p95 < 1s for interactive assistant.
- Cost sensitivity: SMB budget, looking for clear per-token economics, prefer batching/caching recommendations to cut unit costs.
- Models: prefer smaller/fast models for day-to-day; want automatic fallback to cheaper model when cost threshold crossed.

Security/compliance: SOC2 in progress; must support SSO (SAML) for admin console, basic audit logs and retention controls. No on-prem requirement — public cloud ok.

What they tested and observed:
- 2026-03-02: self-serve traffic spike -> 8-12% 429 rate, most errors persisted for 4-6 minutes.
- Team tried exponential backoff but saw significant UX degradation and duplicate processing.
- They looked at competitor docs (OpenAI/Anthropic) for Retry-After usage; want Redwood to publish recommended client backoff config and SDK defaults.

- Transparent quota tiers and documented burst handling semantics (how bursts are smoothed, short-lived burst windows).
- SDKs with built-in backoff + idempotency guidance to avoid duplicate side-effects.
- Option for temporary burst increases during promotions for SMB hosted_api (14-day trial bump).
- Observability: per-route token/call breakdown, 429 dashboards, and alerts for quota exhaustion.
